mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{When solving the heat equation with zero boundary conditions and initial temperature } u(x,0)=f(x), \text{ the coefficients are found by:}\)

mcq.OPT_2: \(\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\)
mcq.OPT_3: \(\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = k \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\)
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{The one-dimensional heat conduction equation for a homogeneous rod is:}\)
\(\text{In steady-state heat conduction, the temperature distribution:}\)
\(\text{For a rod with ends maintained at constant temperatures } \theta_1 \text{ and } \theta_2, \text{ the steady-state temperature distribution is:}\)
\(\text{When solving the heat equation with non-zero boundary conditions, we split the solution as:}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Steady state temperature: } u_s(x) = \frac{100}{l}x.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{New conditions: } u(0,t)=0, u(l,t)=0, u(x,0)=\frac{100}{l}x.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: \frac{100}{l}x = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l \frac{100}{l} x \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx = \frac{200}{n\pi}(-1)^{n+1}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } u(x,t) = \frac{200}{\pi} \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C} \text{ and } 100^\circ\text{C} \text{ until steady state. Then ends are suddenly reduced to } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Steady state before change: } u_s(x) = \frac{50}{l}x + 30.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{New steady state: } u_1(x) = \frac{20}{l}x + 40.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Let } u(x,t)=u_1(x)+u_2(x,t), \text{ where } u_2 \text{ satisfies heat equation with zero ends.}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Boundary conditions for } u_2: u_2(0,t)=0, u_2(l,t)=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Initial condition: } u_2(x,0)=u_s(x)-u_1(x)=\frac{30}{l}x - 10.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Solve for } u_2 \text{ using Fourier sine series: } u_2(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Find } B_n \text{ from } \frac{30}{l}x - 10 = \sum B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}. \text{ Then } u(x,t)=u_1(x)+u_2(x,t).\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has ends kept at } 30^\circ\text{C} \text{ and } 80^\circ\text{C} \text{ until steady state. Then ends are changed to } 40^\circ\text{C} \text{ and } 60^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Initial steady state: \(u_{s1}(x) = 20 + \dfrac{60}{l}x.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Final steady state (after interchange): \(u_{s2}(x) = 80 - \dfrac{60}{l}x.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Let \(u(x,t)= u_{s2}(x) + v(x,t),\) where \(v\) satisfies heat equation with zero BCs.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{BCs for \(v\): \(v(0,t)=0\), \(v(l,t)=0.\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Initial condition: \(u(x,0)= u_{s1}(x) = u_{s2}(x) + v(x,0)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(v(x,0)= u_{s1}(x)-u_{s2}(x) = \left(20+\dfrac{60}{l}x\right) - \left(80-\dfrac{60}{l}x\right) = -60 + \dfrac{120}{l}x.\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Solve for \(v\): \(v(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(B_n = \dfrac{2}{l} \int_0^l \left(-60 + \dfrac{120}{l}x\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Compute: \(B_n = \dfrac{2}{l}\left[ -60 \int_0^l \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx + \dfrac{120}{l} \int_0^l x \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx \right].\) Evaluate integrals to get expression.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Finally \(u(x,t)= 80 - \dfrac{60}{l}x + \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length  $l$  has its ends kept at $20^\circ$ C and $80^\circ$ C until steady state.}\\ \text{Then the temperatures at the ends are interchanged (i.e., $80^\circ$ C at $x=0$ and $20^\circ$ C at $x=l$).}\\ \text{Find the temperature  $u(x,t)$ after the change.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Initial steady state: \(u_{s1}(x)= 50 + 5x\) (since gradient \((100-50)/10=5\)).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Final steady state (after change): \(u_{s2}(x)= 90 - 3x\) (since \((60-90)/10 = -3\), so \(u=90-3x\)).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Let \(u(x,t)= u_{s2}(x) + v(x,t)\), \(v\) satisfies heat equation with zero BCs: \(v(0,t)=0\), \(v(10,t)=0.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Initial: \(u(x,0)= u_{s1}(x)= u_{s2}(x)+v(x,0)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(v(x,0)= u_{s1} - u_{s2} = (50+5x) - (90-3x) = -40 + 8x.\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Solve for \(v\): \(v(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / 100}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(B_n = \dfrac{2}{10} \int_0^{10} (-40+8x) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) dx.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Compute integrals: \(\int \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) dx = -\dfrac{10 \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right)}{n\pi}\), \(\int x \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) dx = \left[ -\dfrac{10x \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right)}{n\pi} + \dfrac{100}{n^2\pi^2} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) \right].\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Combine to get \(B_n.\) Then \(u(x,t)= 90 - 3x + \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / 100}.\)}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length 10 cm has ends $A$ and $B$ kept at $50^\circ$ $C$ and $100^\circ$ $C$ until steady state.}\\ \text{Then the temperature at $A$ is raised to $90^\circ$C and at B is lowered to $60^\circ$C.}\\ \text{Find the subsequent temperature distribution.}\)
